display.purpose: The one huge statement per page, max 11ch.

headline.purpose: Every section h2 and the hero h1, max 15ch, no rule under it; the closing headline alone carries the 120 px copper rule.

title.purpose: Card titles; offer rows, capabilities, people and situations scale it up or down.

metric.purpose: The big numbers in proof, always tabular lining figures; the prices in the offer rows take lining figures only.

body.purpose: Reading text at 16/26, 34 to 56em; cards and offer rows at 17/27.

label.purpose: Mono eyebrows, kickers, years, counts, identifiers and the skills line.

shadows.name: ignition
shadows.purpose: First frame of the mark landing in the header; cools to none over 1.1 s.

shadows.name: metric-burn
shadows.purpose: Text shadow on a big number or the display line arriving ember; cools to ash over 2 s.

shadows.name: card-bloom
shadows.purpose: Copper wash from the top right of a proof card on hover.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: Scroll-driven states: the open capability, the lit step.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: Arrivals: the closing rule, the wall detail, an answer opening. Exits run faster.

motion.name: ease-in-out-cubic
motion.purpose: The hero canvas: stroke drawing and the flight of the rune to the header.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Colour changes on links and buttons; a press answers in .1s.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Situation row hover: the title goes hot copper.

motion.name: underline
motion.value: transform .45s ease-house, scaleX from 0 at the left

motion.name: ignite
motion.value: 1.1s to 2s ease-out, ember to copper or ash, glow to none
motion.purpose: Hero ignition that settles over 1.6 s to a faint resting halo, mark landing, metric burn.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every mark finished, every section static, no reveal.

narrative.overview:
Dark iron ground and one copper element that has just cooled. The page is a large, exact, unhurried surface: oversized Schibsted Grotesk headings on long measures, hairlines instead of boxes, IBM Plex Mono for the small labels that date and number things, and copper as the only colour. Nothing moves unless the scroll asks it to, and when it does, the movement is a single idea: copper heats to ember, flares, and cools back to copper within two seconds. The mark is the only thing on the page that was ever hot.

The mark is Fehu drawn as the counterform of a square, four solid pieces and three channels, read as a geometric symbol first and a rune second. It carries the whole identity: it draws itself in the hero, lands in the header, becomes the diagram of what we build, and reassembles in the closing scene. Everything else defers to it.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only on the site. Iron ground, slate surfaces, seam hairlines.

Copper is the single accent and it is spent sparingly: the mark, links, the primary button, prices, the lit marker and one emphasis per section. Labels, bullets, kickers and indices are smoke or steel.
Type does the structure. Headings at 78 to 132 px with tight tracking, body at 16/26, mono labels at 12 to 13 px.

Copper light is part of the system and always cools: the rune ignites once and settles to copper with a faint resting halo, the one light the page keeps at rest; the mark flashes as it lands, a metric burns in and cools, and a proof card blooms on hover.

Blocks arrive as the scroll reaches them: a 24 px rise and fade over 0.7 s, 60 ms later for each item in a group. No count-up, no panel that shrinks or dims, no pointer-following light or tilt. Scroll-driven scenes on desktop become static, single-column sections under 900 px and under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The One Metal Rule
rules.body: Copper is the only hue on the page. Status colours from the master system (success, warning, error) are reserved for documents and tools and do not appear on the site.

rules.name: The Cooling Rule
rules.body: Ember appears only as the start of a transition that ends in copper or ash. If an element is ember or glowing after two seconds, it is a defect.

rules.name: The Text-on-Copper Rule
rules.body: Text on a copper fill is always iron, never ash and never white.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every metric and every column of numbers sets tabular lining figures; a single price inside an offer row sets lining figures only, so a decimal point keeps its natural width.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase styling anywhere, including labels and buttons.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Headings stop at 15ch, display at 11ch, reading text between 34 and 56em. Use max-width in ch or em, not pixels.

rules.name: The Lit-by-State Rule
rules.body: Glow belongs to a transition: arrival, ignition, a hover bloom. A held state (the open capability, the selected name, the lit word) is marked by colour alone. Nothing at rest shows a glow or a grey shadow, except the hero rune's faint resting halo. The system has no grey shadow at all.

rules.name: The Copper Light Rule
rules.body: Every glow is copper, hot copper or ember at some alpha. There is no white glow and no coloured shadow of any other hue.

dos: Do keep copper as the only hue: mark, links, primary button, lit markers, one emphasis per section.
Do build structure from type and hairlines: headlines at 78 px and up, seam rules between rows, no boxes around text.
Do use tabular lining figures on every metric and every column of numbers; a lone price sets lining figures only.
Do let copper light mark a transition only: ignite at ember, cool to copper or ash within two seconds, bloom on hover. Held states are marked by colour.
Do use the house ease, cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1), for the transitions that remain: the title rule, the open capability, the wall detail, the questions.
Do show every mark finished and every section static under prefers-reduced-motion, and check Safari after any canvas change.
Do collapse to one column at 900 px, drop three- and four-column grids to two at 1100 px, and unpin every scene on small screens.
donts: Don't put a glow, a grey shadow or a gradient on a surface at rest.
Don't add a second accent, a status colour, purple, neon green, or any white glow.
Don't rotate the mark, recolour a piece, round its corners, fill a channel, or place it on a photograph.
Don't use runic alphabets as decoration, Norse imagery, hexagons, chains and nodes, circuit patterns, isometric cubes, stock photography or emoji.
Don't set anything in uppercase, use a pill, a corner above 4 px, a border heavier than 1 px, or a font other than Schibsted Grotesk and IBM Plex Mono.
Don't write an em dash or an exclamation mark anywhere, including code comments.
